added_lines: the council is approaching the end of its four year term. we dis cussed the protocol for selecting a new council. it was noted that the criteria for sel ecting candidates is that they should have the time to give to the council. they should be able to think in terms of the whole parish (some find it hard to see b eyond a particular area of interest) they should be team players, able to work well with others, good listeners, interested in other views and perspectives; they need to see beyond their own preoccupations. they should be open of new ways of doing things, with an energy and passion about the future of the parish. they should be able to work by way of meetings—planning, discussing, reviewing. (many people who are “doers” find meetings intolerable). attention will also given to having a council that is representative of the church areas of the paris h, of gender equality, particular skills needed by the council, and age profile. national synod the irish synodal pathway began in 2021 when the bishops of ireland invited the church to embark on a process of renewal inviting people throughout the church to engage in prayer, listening and reflection, and to reflect o n important questions about the identity and mission of the church in ireland, including its pastoral life, structures, relationships, ministry and place in society. through this process, baptism emerged as a foundational lens for understanding the identity and mission of the church, leading to seven priorities: belon ging; co- responsibility and lay ministry; family; formation and catechesis ; healing; women; and youth. following the pre-synodal assembly in kilkenny in october 2025, working groups were established to deepen this discernment and develop practical proposals. these 35 proposals were subsequently grouped under five path ways and presented in the working document – is not this what god asks of you? : – the church that proclaims the gospel – the church as a community of belonging – the church as a place of healing – the church that accompanies, – the church that empowers for ministry and co-responsibility.

or email sligoleitrim@alcoholfor um.com you don’t have to be addicted to suffer from addiction! our policy regarding children in our parish churches? if your kids are loud, please still come to church. if you're running late because getting everyone out the door was a battle, please still come to church. if your toddler won't sit still, please still come to church. if your baby needs to eat, please still come to church. if your child asks questions at the least convenient time, please still come to church. if someone cries, drops a toy, needs a snack, or has to make their third trip to the bathroom, please still come to church. if your child doesn't know all the words, all the prayers, or exactly when to sit and stand, please still come to church if you feel like you spent the entire mass managing your children and heard approximately 12% of the sermon, please still come to church. if sunday morning feels messy instead of peaceful, please still come to church if you're worried about, if you're worried your children are distracting the people around you, please still come to church. because children do not learn how to be part of the church by staying home they can sit quietly. they learn by being here. they learn the singing by hearing us sing. they learn the prayers by hearing us pray. they learn to worship by watching us worship. they learn that church is home because we make room for them here.

hence derives the pious custom of suffrage for the souls of the faithful departed , which is an urgent supplication of god to have mercy on souls of the dead, to purify them by the fire of his charity, and to bring to his kingdom of light and life. this suffrage is a cultic expression of faith in the communion of saints. indeed, the church in its pilgrim members, from the earliest days of chr istian religion, has honoured with great respect the memory of the dead; and ‘because it is a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead that they may be loosed from their sins’(2 mac 12:46) she offers her suffrages for them. these consist primarily, in the celebration of the holy sacrifice of the eucharist, and in other pious exercises, such as prayers for the dead, alms deeds, works of m ercy, and the application of indulgences to the souls of the faithful departed . directory on popular piety and the liturgy, 249-52
